title: Policy transpiler & config contract validator for region/tier routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Refactor the routing policy evaluation pipeline by introducing a policy transpiler that converts high-level DSL rules (region selectors, tier routing, fallback model variants) into a canonical, strongly-typed contract consumed by the runtime. This ticket focuses on schema and contract validation for the DSL, a linter that surfaces ambiguous rules at config-time, and a staged migration path for existing policy documents. Goals: (1) Define a backward-compatible canonical policy schema with explicit region and tier primitives, priority/fallback ordering, and model-compatibility annotations; (2) Implement a transpiler that emits typed policy artifacts and human-friendly validation errors; (3) Add a config linter and CI checks to prevent unsafe or ambiguous policy changes; (4) Provide a migration tool to rewrite legacy routing docs into the new canonical form and a compatibility mode in the runtime for 3 sprints. Non-goals: runtime execution engine rewrite (only schema + contract outputs), UI redesign for Console (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical policy schema (JSON Schema + typed AST reference) is checked into docs/policy/canonical-schema.md and includes fields for region selector, tier, capacity hints, and fallback variants.
Transpiler CLI exists (redwood-policy-transpile) that takes legacy DSL files and emits canonical JSON policy artifacts with human-readable warnings for lossy rewrites.
Config linter integrated into CI returns non-zero for ambiguous rules (e.g., overlapping region selectors without explicit precedence) and provides actionable messages.
A suite of unit tests covers AST -> canonical contract transformations and edge cases: wildcard regions, overlapping tiers, missing model fallbacks.
End-to-end smoke test demonstrating a canary rollout where policy fallback triggers a compatible model variant in another region under simulated capacity pressure.
Migration docs and a short runbook for operators describing compatibility mode, rollback steps, and common remediation patterns are published.
No user-facing downtime during rollout in staging; runtime compatibility mode passes integration tests against existing policy examples from customers (sample set: 18 configs).
